item.title: The Vikings swung and missed in effort to find a franchise quarterback
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: After the 2023 season, the Vikings decided to abandon the veteran quarterback rollercoaster for a potential franchise quarterback.
item.content:encoded:
After the 2023 season, the Vikings decided to abandon the veteran quarterback rollercoaster for a potential franchise quarterback.

The ride ended up being bumper cars without the bumpers.

Minnesota had earned the 11th overall pick in the 2024 draft. Four quarterbacks had been drafted in the first eight picks. As the clock ticked toward their pick at No. 11, the Vikings feared being leapfrogged by the Broncos at No. 12.

And so the Vikings gave up a fourth-round pick and a fifth-round pick to move up from No. 11 to No. 10. (They also received a seventh-rounder from the Jets as part of the deal.) They used the pick not to take Oregon quarterback Bo Nix, but to select Michigan quarterback J.J. McCarthy.

His rookie season was lost to a meniscus injury during the preseason opener. And while the 2024 season went well with free-agent Sam Darnold stepping in, the Vikings opted to go all-in with McCarthy for 2025, allowing both Darnold and Daniel Jones to leave via free agency.

McCarthy won his debut game on a Monday night in Chicago. A Week 2 loss in Atlanta resulted in an ankle injury that caused McCarthy to miss the next five games. He returned in Week 9 with an upset of the Lions in Detroit. Three straight losses followed, and a concussion in Green Bay caused McCarthy to miss what was a 26-0 low point in Seattle with undrafted rookie Max Brosmer at the helm.

But then McCarthy returned. He won three in a row, missed the Christmas Day win over the Lions (Brosmer got a little redemption, but not much, in the defense-driven performance), and won the regular-season finale against the Packers. While the Vikings' postseason hopes were dashed after the shutout loss to the Seahawks, the Vikings finished strong under McCarthy.

Still, the two-year body of work wasn't enough to keep the Vikings from pouncing on the opportunity to add Kyler Murray in free agency, on a bargain-basement deal (thanks to the Cardinals owing him more than $35 million in 2026). The competition between Murray and McCarthy lingered into training camp, with Murray getting the job in the days before the preseason opener.

At that point, it seemed that a fresh start for McCarthy would be beneficial for both sides. The vibes were clearly off, even though the team and the player did their best to conceal any dysfunction. The fact that McCarthy slipped behind Carson Wentz on the depth chart underscored the reality that it was just a matter of time before McCarthy would be gone.

Opportunity knocked after the Giants lost Jaxson Dart to a knee injury. Still, the Vikings got merely a fifth-round pick for McCarthy — after giving up the 11th pick in 2024, a fourth-round pick, and a fifth-round pick to get him (with the seventh-round pick in return).

It's always prudent for a team that has made a mistake to admit it and move on. Doubling down helps no one. Still, there's a price to be paid for acknowledging to such a major blunder.

And while no one knows what was happening behind the scenes, the early-season performances from Murray and Wentz suggested that maybe, at some point in 2026, the Vikings would have needed McCarthy to play. His absence puts more pressure on the team to make it work with Murray and/or Wentz (and, if necessary, with Brosmer).

The Vikings also need to quietly hope that McCarthy doesn't become a competent contributor for the Giants. If he does, the Vikings would join the list of franchises that used a high pick on a rookie quarterback, failed to develop him, and folded the tents prematurely.

item.title: Giants to waive QB Jake Haener, intend to re-sign him to practice squad
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: With the Giants trading for J.J.
item.content:encoded:
With the Giants trading for J.J. McCarthy, the club will make another roster move to keep just two quarterbacks on their 53-man roster.

Per Mike Garafolo of NFL Network, New York will waive Jake Haener but intend to re-sign him to the team's practice squad.

Haener was promoted to the active roster on Saturday after Jaxson Dart suffered a long-term knee injury last Monday night.

Haener, 27, joined the Giants in August after spending some time with the Chiefs during the offseason program.

A fourth-round pick in 2023, Haener has appeared in eight career games with one start. All of his appearances came in 2024 with the Saints.

item.title: Todd Bowles: Baker Mayfield out a minimum of three weeks with thumb dislocation
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: There is more clarity on Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield after he suffered a dislocated thumb late in Sunday’s loss to the Vikings.
item.content:encoded:
There is more clarity on Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield after he suffered a dislocated thumb late in Sunday’s loss to the Vikings.

Head coach Todd Bowles told reporters in his Monday press conference that Mayfield will be out for a minimum of three weeks.

“It’s consistent with everything we thought it was — a dislocation,” Bowles said.

According to multiple reporters on the Bucs beat, further tests on Mayfield’s thumb did not reveal a fracture or ligament damage.

With the current timetable, the Buccaneers are not planning on placing Mayfield on injured reserve right now. But that could change. If the Bucs were to put Mayfield on IR, he’d be out for a minimum of four games.

Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels is set to become the starter in Mayfield’s absence.

“Well it’s going to be like every other rookie, but he’s played well in the preseason,” Bowles said. “He’s very bright. He’s not going to be out there by himself — there will be 22 other guys out there helping him out. So, we’re just expecting him to do his job, play at a high level, as he expects from himself.”

Bowles added that the Buccaneers will likely add either a veteran or a practice squad quarterback. Only Mayfield and Daniels are on the 53-man roster with Easton Stick on the practice squad.

item.title: Panthers CB Jaycee Horn to miss significant time with a quad injury
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Panthers got good news about wide receiver Jalen Coker's quad injury, but cornerback Jaycee Horn did not fare as well.
item.content:encoded:
The Panthers got good news about wide receiver Jalen Coker's quad injury, but cornerback Jaycee Horn did not fare as well.

Horn also hurt his quad during Carolina's 21-18 loss to the Browns and multiple reports on Monday say that he has suffered a significant injury. It is believed to be a tear and Horn could be out for the rest of the season depending on what he hears as he solicits more opinions about the injury.

Horn signed a four-year extension with the team this offseason, so his future with the club is secure even if he can't make it back on the field before the end of the season. He had six tackles and two pass breakups in his three appearances this year.

Mike Jackson, Akayleb Evans and rookie Will Lee also saw time at corner on Sunday.

item.title: Davante Adams: 1-2 start is "nothing to freak out about"
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: When Davante Adams was a rookie on the Packers — way back in 2014 — the team got off to a 1-2 start.
item.content:encoded:
When Davante Adams was a rookie on the Packers — way back in 2014 — the team got off to a 1-2 start.

Green Bay’s quarterback then famously spelled out a word during a radio interview: “R-E-L-A-X.”

Eventually, that Packers team went 12-4 in the regular season, beat the Cowboys in the divisional round, and lost a wild NFC Championship game to the Seahawks.

It’s over a decade later, but perhaps that was somewhere in the back of Adams’ mind on Sunday night after the Rams lost to the Broncos, dropping Los Angeles’ record to 1-2.

“Stay in, I mean, it’s nothing to freak out about,” Adams said, via transcript from the Broncos, when asked about the team’s 1-2 start. “There’s a lot of football left, and it’s not like we’re not playing good ball, obviously excluding that first game.

“Unfortunately, I mean, I don’t know if it’s unfortunate, but based on our situation, unfortunately, this league is about wins and losses, so there’s a lot that we can take from a game like this and feel good about. But there’s no moral victories, so we’re definitely disappointed to not finish it out. But just to get back to what we do, and that’s going back to practice, get back to the drawing board and just find a way to finish off something again.”

With Puka Nacua sidelined for the last couple of weeks due to injury, Adams has been the team’s top receiving option — recording back-to-back games of 100 yards for the first time since joining the team last offseason.

While Nacua may be back for Week 4, the schedule will not get any easier, as the Rams will travel across the country to face the Eagles on Sunday.

item.title: Vikings send J.J. McCarthy to the Giants for a 2027 fifth-round pick
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Minnesota send 10th pick in 2024 to New York.
item.content:encoded:
The J.J. McCarthy experiment in Minnesota has ended. In New York, it's just beginning.

Per multiple reports, the Vikings have traded the tenth overall pick in the 2024 draft to the Giants. In return, the Vikings will receive a 2027 fifth-round pick.

The Giants have a clear need at the position, given the knee injury that will keep Jaxson Dart out for at least the rest of the regular season. On Sunday, the starter was Jameis Winston, with Jake Haener as the understudy.

In Minnesota, McCarthy lost the starting job to Kyler Murray before falling behind Carson Wentz to the third spot on the depth chart. From the moment McCarthy was benched, it seemed that he was on borrowed time in Minnesota — even though everyone involved was saying all the right things.

For the Giants, the move brings the former Michigan quarterback (coached by Jim Harbaugh) to the NFL team coached by John Harbaugh.

For now, Winston is the starter. Whether McCarthy gets an opportunity to play depends on whether Winston is injured — and whether Winston remains sufficiently effective.

item.title: Mike Vrabel: Drake Maye needs to "relax"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: A year after finishing second in the NFL MVP voting, Patriots quarterback Drake Maye won't have to worry about nearly missing out on the award in 2026.
item.content:encoded:
A year after finishing second in the NFL MVP voting, Patriots quarterback Drake Maye won't have to worry about nearly missing out on the award in 2026.

Through three games of the the third season his career, Maye has regressed. Badly.

Last year, he had 31 touchdown passes and eight interceptions. This year, he has one touchdown pass and six interceptions. His passer rating has plummeted from 113.5 to 58.6.

Sunday's 35-6 disaster in Duval included three turnovers and no touchdowns.

Appearing Monday on WEEI's The Greg Hill Show, coach Mike Vrabel was asked about Maye's obvious issues with decision-making.

“I think quarterbacks want to make plays," Vrabel said, via Mike Reiss of ESPN. "I think they want to throw touchdowns. I think sometimes when Greg and I go golfing, we really want to make a good score, right? Sometimes we’re so focused on it, we try to choke the life out of the golf club, and we’re squeezing it so damn tight that the ball has no choice but to go sideways. We need to stop trying to choke the life out of every single play. We need to relax. We need to settle in and go play football and not try to force things that aren’t there.”

It seems at this point to be more than bad decisions. Simms explained on Monday's PFT Live that Maye has developed mechanical flaws, including a flicking of the wrist before the makes his throws. Also, Simms believes Maye is trying too hard to guide his throws, in lieu of letting it rip.

If the Patriots agree with the assessment, it won't be easy to coach these things out of Maye during football season, when there's a fresh train always heading down the tracks. And the next stop is Buffalo.

Last year in Week 5, Maye led the Patriots to a win in their final game at the Bills' old stadium. This year in Week 4, Maye has a chance to reverse a troubling trend that has become a full-blown narrative.

item.title: Dexter Lawrence: Our goal wasn't to go undefeated, we'll own this one
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Through two games, the Bengals’ defense looked like it had undergone a significant transformation in the offseason — partially due to the addition of Dexter Lawrence.
item.content:encoded:
Through two games, the Bengals’ defense looked like it had undergone a significant transformation in the offseason — partially due to the addition of Dexter Lawrence.

But then came Sunday’s divisional matchup against the Steelers, with Pittsburgh’s offense generating 411 yards — including 138 on the ground — en route to defeating Cincinnati 30-27.

Lawrence, in his eighth pro season, provided some perspective after the game.

“I think it's a reminder to show y'all that we’re not going to go undefeated,” Lawrence said, via Jay Morrison of SI.com. “No year is gonna be perfect. … Our goal wasn’t to go undefeated. So we’ll own this one. We'll come back next week and go out there and play.”

Lawrence added that Sunday’s performance “wasn’t us.”

“We know we can't allow that; however it comes, however they try to do it,” Lawrence said. “We made a lot of mistakes, and that's what kept the game close and then ultimately helped them win.

“A lot of what was going on was self-inflicted. … You watched the game. You know what happened. I don't think it was anything special that they had going on. We just didn't do well on our end.”

The Bengals will get another tough opponent next week when the Jaguars come to Cincinnati.

item.title: Mekhi Becton worked out for the Packers, will sign with the team
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Packers signed guard Laken Tomlinson after last Thursday's loss to the Falcons and they may not be done adding to their offensive line options.
item.content:encoded:
The Packers signed guard Laken Tomlinson after last Thursday's loss to the Falcons and they may not be done adding to their offensive line options.

Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reports that they had Mekhi Becton in for a workout on Monday morning.

Becton signed a two-year deal with the Chargers as a free agent in 2025, but he was released in March. He started 14 games during his one season with the team and was the Eagles' right guard when they won the Super Bowl the previous year.

Becton also has experience at tackle during his time with the Jets. He was picked in the first round by the Jets in 2020 and spent four years with the team, but missed all but one game in 2021 and 2022 due to injuries.

UPDATE 11:39 a.m. ET: Fowler reports that Becton will sign with the Packers.

item.title: Report: Jalen Coker questionable for Week 4 with a quad strain
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Panthers wide receiver Jalen Coker was able to play on Sunday after being listed as questionable due to an ankle injury, but a different injury brought his day to an early end.
item.content:encoded:
Panthers wide receiver Jalen Coker was able to play on Sunday after being listed as questionable due to an ankle injury, but a different injury brought his day to an early end.

Coker left the 21-18 loss to the Browns in the third quarter after injuring his quad. Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that Coker has a relatively minor strain and that he is considered questionable to play against the Lions on Sunday night in Week 4 as a result.

Panthers cornerback Jaycee Horn also suffered a quad injury on Sunday and head coach Dave Canales said after the game that he still needs to be evaluated.

Coker had two catches for 18 yards on Sunday. He has 18 catches for 222 yards and two touchdowns on the season.

item.title: Bills overcome five turnovers to defeat Chargers, 24-16
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: While it was ugly for much of the afternoon, Buffalo was still able to defeat Los Angeles and move to 3-0.
item.content:encoded:
It’s not often that a team can turn the ball over five times and win.

But that’s exactly what happened in Buffalo on Sunday, with the Bills coming from behind to defeat the Chargers 24-16.

Los Angeles was able to get off to a 10-0 lead after a fumble from James Cook on the first play from scrimmage and an interception on Buffalo’s third drive.

But the Bills were able to tie it up at 10-10 with Josh Allen’s 1-yard touchdown run late in the second quarter. Allen had set it up with a 37-yard pass to Keon Coleman with little time before the break.

The Bills had three turnovers in the first half. While they had two more fumbles in the second half, the Chargers punted after one and Justin Herbert threw an interception deep in the red zone on the second.

Josh Allen powered his way in for another 1-yard touchdown with 7:35 left in the contest to give the Bills their first lead of the day. Then James Cook was actually allowed to run in a touchdown, taking it in from 3 yards out to put the game away.

Aside from his fumble, Cook had an excellent day — rushing for 154 yards on 24 carries with his TD.

Allen finished 16-of-26 for 204 yards with two interceptions and a lost fumble. He had 22 yards on eight carries with two TDs.

On the other side, Herbert was 20-of-34 for 226 yards with a touchdown and an interception.

That was Los Angeles’ lone giveaway of the game, but the +4 advantage in turnover margin was not enough.

With the victory, the Bills are now 3-0. They’ll stay at home to host the Patriots next Sunday.

The Chargers are 0-3 and staring down the barrel of a long season. They will be on the road to face the defending-champion Seahawks next Sunday.

item.title: Despite 1-2 start, Rams remain favorites to win the Super Bowl
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: A disappointing start to the season hasn't changed the Rams' status as the Super Bowl favorites.
item.content:encoded:
A disappointing start to the season hasn't changed the Rams' status as the Super Bowl favorites.

After Sunday night's loss to the Broncos dropped the Rams' record to 1-2, the Rams remain the betting favorites to win it all.

The Rams' current odds are +650, which are down from their +500 odds before the season, but still the best odds in the league to win the title.

Although the Rams haven't looked like a Super Bowl team yet, it will be hard to bet against them in January if Myles Garrett and Puka Nacua are healthy, and Aaron Donald looks like the Aaron Donald of old.

After the Rams, the next-best odds to win it all go to the Bills, at +700. They're followed by the 49ers and Ravens, both at +900, the Seahaks at +1000, the Chiefs at +1100, the Eagles at +1500, the Bengals at +1700, the Lions at +1900 and the Broncos at +2000.

item.title: De'Von Achane out for season with torn ACL
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Achane exited Sunday's game against the Chiefs in the first quarter.
item.content:encoded:
The Dolphins will not have one of their best players for the rest of the season.

Running back De'Von Achane suffered a torn ACL during Sunday's loss to the Chiefs, according to a joint report from ESPN and NFL Network.

Head coach Jeff Hafley told reporters in his postgame press conference that news about Achane’s injury did not sound optimistic.

Achane went down during the first quarter of Sunday’s contest after recording an 11-yard reception. He was tackled awkwardly before coming off the field gingerly under his own power.

The Dolphins signed Achane to a four-year $64 million contract extension during the offseason.

Achane led the league with 5.7 yards per carry last season, rushing for 1,350 yards with eight touchdowns. He also caught 67 passes for 488 yards with four TDs in 2025.

A third-round pick in 2023, Achane has appeared in 47 career games with 39 starts. He’s rushed for 3,184 yards with 22 touchdowns and caught 179 passes for 1,326 yards with 13 TDs.

item.title: Marcus Mariota and the Commanders stun the Seahawks 33-31
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: A massive upset in Washington as the defending champions lose for the first time this season.
item.content:encoded:
No Jayden Daniels? No problem for the Commanders today, as backup quarterback Marcus Mariota turned in an incredible effort against the stout Seahawks' defense, leading Washington to a 33-31 win.

Mariota sealed the Commanders' win with a nine-yard run on third-and-7 with 1:15 remaining, and that was just the last of a number of spectacular plays by Mariota, who played very well against this Seahawks defense that has shut down so many quarterbacks over the last two years.

The 32-year-old Mariota finished 19 of 31 for 183 yards, with three touchdowns and no interceptions.

Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold returned from his Week 1 injury and completed 31 of 45 passes for 379 yards, with four touchdowns and two interceptions. Jaxon Smith-Njigba was, as usual, Darnold's favorite receiver, with 10 catches for 128 yards and two touchdowns.

Today's game serves to show just how unpredictable the NFL is, especially early in the season, when there is still so much we don't know about every team. The Seahawks opened the season 2-0 and looking like perhaps the best team in the NFL. The Commanders entered today 0-2 and, without Daniels, looked like one of the worst teams in the NFL. But that's why they play the games.

item.title: Ravens beat Cowboys 34-31 on final play in Brazil
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Ravens had only 7 seconds when they got the ball back, but one play got Tyler Loop in position for 56-yard FG.
item.content:encoded:
In one of the most exciting games of the season, the Ravens pulled out a miraculous 34-31 victory over the Cowboys on the final play in Brazil.

Kicker Tyler Loop, who grew up in the Dallas area and had to live the offseason with a missed kick that ultimately kept the Ravens out of the playoffs, nailed a 56-yarder with no time left.

After a touchback on the kickoff, the Ravens got the ball back with only seven seconds left. But Lamar Jackson worked his magic, connecting with Zay Flowers for a 27-yard gain to the Cowboys 38. The Ravens got a timeout with one second left.

It was the third lead change in the final two minutes and improved the Ravens' record to 2-1 and dropped the Cowboys to 1-2.

First, Ravens rookie tight end Matt Hibner scored on a 2-yard pass from Jackson on third down to give Baltimore a 31-28 lead. It was too much time for Dak Prescott and the Cowboys.

Dallas got a gift from the officials on the nine-play, 60-yard drive.

Ravens cornerback Nate Wiggins was in position for an interception with 23 seconds left, but Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb hooked Wiggins' arm. The CBS crew argued that it should have been offensive pass interference. Instead, officials threw the flag on Wiggins, giving the Cowboys the ball at the 2.

A false start on tight end Luke Schoonmaker kept the Cowboys from a game-winning touchdown with two Prescott incompletions sandwiched between a 2-yard scramble.

Brandon Aubrey kicked a chip-shot, 23-yard field goal with seven seconds left. That proved too much time for Jackson and the Ravens.

The Cowboys stopped the Ravens twice on fourth down, and the Ravens stopped the Cowboys once on fourth down. The Cowboys had a field goal blocked and lost a controversial fumble that looked like it might have been an incompletion.

The Cowboys outgained the Ravens 415 to 378 yards.

Jackson was 15-of-20 for 186 yards and two touchdowns and ran for 50 yards on six carries. Zay Flowers catching five passes for 84 yards. Derrick Henry rushed for 89 yards and two touchdowns on 26 carries.

Prescott went 25-of-40 for 276 yards and a touchdown. Lamb caught seven passes for 112 yards and George Pickens added seven receptions for 82 yards. Javonte Williams rushed for 98 yards and a touchdown on 19 carries.

Both teams had a number of significant injuries.

The Ravens lost their top two centers late in the game, with both carted to the training room. The absences of Jovaughn Gwyn (ankle) and Ethan Pocic (knee) forced rookie right guard Olaivavega Ioane to move to center.

item.title: Aaron Rodgers wins quarterback duel with Joe Burrow, Steelers beat Bengals 30-27
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Both quarterbacks played well, but Burrow's late fumble sealed the Bengals' loss.
item.content:encoded:
Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers and Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow battled for 60 minutes today, but a Burrow fumble in the final minute sealed it.

With the Steelers leading 30-27 but the Bengals driving with 53 seconds left, Burrow was sacked and fumbled, the Steelers recovered, and Pittsburgh won at home.

Rodgers completed 19 of 34 passes for 292 yards, with three touchdowns and one interception, a very different game than he had in the first two weeks of this season. Through two games, Rodgers looked old and unreliable, but today he came to life with an outstanding performance.

Burrow completed 28 of 37 passes for 282 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions, but that late fumble will haunt him. Steelers running back Jaylen Warren had 17 carries for 127 yards, and he almost had a much bigger game, but an 87-yard run was called back by a DK Metcalf holding penalty.

The Steelers' win leaves both teams at 2-1 and tied for the lead in what looks like it will be a very competitive AFC North. If Rodgers can keep playing like he did today, the Steelers are going to be playoff contenders.

item.title: Chiefs take Dolphins' best punch, but move to 3-0 with 24-10 win
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: The Dolphins were plenty competitive against the Chiefs for much of Sunday afternoon.
item.content:encoded:
The Dolphins were plenty competitive against the Chiefs for much of Sunday afternoon.

But Kansas City’s fourth-down defense proved to be a separator, allowing the club to come away with a 24-10 victory in South Florida.

While Miami was able to sustain drives and gain plenty of yards, the club was 0-of-3 on fourth down with chances to pick up points. The Chiefs also picked up a key takeaway to halt a drive in the second quarter.

With the score at 17-10 midway through the fourth quarter, Miami elected to go for it on fourth-and-5 from their own 48 with 6:00 left on the clock. But Malik Willis’ pass was incomplete, setting up the Chiefs with good field position.

Kansas City took advantage of it, with Patrick Mahomes connecting with Travis Kelce for an 11-yard touchdown to put the game out of reach with 2:55 left in the contest.

The Dolphins elected to go for it again on fourth down on their ensuing drive, but Chris Jones tipped Willis’ pass, and George Karlaftis came down with it for an interception to effectively end the game, though Harrison Butker missed a 50-yard field goal that would have given the club three more points.

Mahomes was 20-of-24 for 246 yards with two touchdowns and an interception. The pick went right off Rashee Rice’s hands and was tipped by another defender before Miami came down with the takeaway. Rice ended up leading the Chiefs with 88 yards on seven receptions.

Kelce had two catches for 59 yards with his TD.

On the other side, Willis was 20-of-36 for 210 yards with an interception. He also was the leading rusher with 56 yards on nine attempts.

The Dolphins played most of the game without De’Von Achane, who exited the contest with a knee injury on the first drive.

With the victory, Mahomes has 115 wins in his first 150 starts. That mark is tied with Tom Brady for No. 1 all-time, ahead of Joe Montana’s 108.

It’s Kansas City’s fifth 3-0 start since Mahomes became the team’s starter in 2018.

The Chiefs will be in Las Vegas next week to take on the division-rival Raiders.

The Dolphins will also be on the road in Week 4, facing the Vikings.

item.title: Deshaun Watson: I just wanted to finish the game for the fans
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Browns fans booed Deshaun Watson in the second half of a preseason game against the Bills.
item.content:encoded:
Browns fans booed Deshaun Watson in the second half of a preseason game against the Bills. On Sunday, they cheered him.

Watson threw a 14-yard touchdown pass to tight end Harold Fannin Jr. with 1:48 left to lift the Browns to a 21-18 upset of the Panthers. He finished with 144 yards and two touchdowns, along with 45 yards rushing on 11 carries.

Winning makes everyone happy.

"It was great. It was amazing. I just wanted to finish the job for them," Watson said of the fans, via Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN. "There was one moment where I got a little teary-eyed, feeling that energy. I've put in so much work to get here, to be in this moment here and to be able to show I can finish these drives, and finish these games to get W's for this city and this organization.

"This is what all the hard work, belief, prayers, everything that I have put myself through the last 22 months. To be able to stand in front of the crowd on that field and to finish the job. I want to keep improving and keep trying to get better each and every day, each week and we have a big one on Thursday [against the Steelers]."

After the home fans booed him last month, Watson made it worse by calling it "disrespectful" and "personal." He apologized a few days later, saying his "emotions got the best of me."

The only way to win them over was to play well and win, and Watson has done both.

The Browns are tied for first place with the other three teams in the division at 2-1, and Watson has completed 63.8 percent of his passes for 587 yards with five touchdowns and one interception. He also has run for 105 yards.

He is the first Browns quarterback since Baker Mayfield in Weeks 14 and 15 of 2018 to lead game-winning touchdown drives in the fourth quarter of consecutive games, according to ESPN Research.

"We continued to feed off that energy of the crowd, and we wanted to make a special play," Watson said. "I told the guys in the huddle, 'Man, just [believe] in me and I'm going to use my legs.' Whenever that play comes up, make that play, and Harold did."

item.title: Travis Hunter: "Little bit" of relief to get first interception
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Jaguars head coach Liam Coen's talk about giving Travis Hunter more to do in Week 3 didn't result in a major change to his role, but the 2025 first-round pick was able to check off one career milestone.
item.content:encoded:
Jaguars head coach Liam Coen's talk about giving Travis Hunter more to do in Week 3 didn't result in a major change to his role, but the 2025 first-round pick was able to check off one career milestone.

Hunter had the first interception of his NFL career while playing cornerback late in the first half. Hunter snagged a pass from Patriots quarterback Drake Maye to wide receiver Efton Chism in the end zone to keep the Jaguars up 14-3.

The Jags went on to win 35-6 and Hunter, who also had four tackles, was asked after the game if it was a relief to finally get his first pick.

"A little bit," Hunter said. "Interceptions are great to catch, but I was focused on winning the game and just continue to focus on the next play."

Hunter played five offensive snaps at wide receiver during the game and did not have a catch, but his hands served him well in his other role.

item.title: Kirk Cousins throws 3 TDs, Raiders move to 3-0 with 35-27 victory over Saints
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: For just the second time since 2002, the Raiders are 3-0.
item.content:encoded:
For just the second time since 2002, the Raiders are 3-0.

After entering the fourth quarter down 27-22, Las Vegas picked up four takeaways in the final period to defeat New Orleans 35-27.

While the Raiders held a 16-13 lead at halftime, the Saints were able to score twice in quick succession in the third quarter to ostensibly take control of the game. Tyler Shough threw a 1-yard touchdown pass to Juwan Johnson before the Raiders fumbled the ensuing kickoff. Shough then connected with Noah Fant for a 16-yard score to put New Orleans up 27-16 with 5:46 left in the third quarter.

But it was all Las Vegas from there. Mike Washington scored on a 36-yard touchdown run to cap a quick, five-play drive. The two-point conversion failed, keeping the score at 27-22, New Orleans.

That’s when the turnovers began, with Shough losing the ball on a strip-sack in Las Vegas territory on third-and-4 from the Las Vegas 29.

Kirk Cousins hit Cody White for a 4-yard touchdown to give the Raiders a 28-27 lead with 9:21 left in regulation.

Down by one, Shough then threw an interception that set up Cousins’ 4-yard touchdown to Brock Bowers — who was making his 2026 debut — for a 35-27 lead.

For the Saints’ third turnover, Shough was again strip-sacked with 2:21 left in regulation on fourth-and-1 deep in Las Vegas territory.

And while the team got the ball back, Johnson fumbled with just under a minute left, and the Raiders recovered to clinch their victory.

Sunday’s win was the first time the Raiders scored at least 30 points since defeating the Chargers 63-21 on a Thursday night in December 2023.

As noted by the CBS broadcast, the game also tied an NFL record with six touchdown receptions by tight ends. The only other time that had happened was in 1981 in a matchup between the Chargers and Raiders.

Cousins finished 22-of-33 for 248 yards with three touchdowns. That makes him the first QB in team history to record at least three passing TDs in each of the club’s first three games. He’s also the first since Lamar Jackson in 2022 to record at least three passing TDs in each of his team’s first three games.

After undergoing a meniscus trim, Bowers was as excellent as ever, catching 10 passes on 13 targets for 116 yards with a TD.

On the other side, Shough finished 29-of-42 for 255 yards with four touchdowns, an interception, and two lost fumbles. Chris Olave led with nine catches for 107 yards.

At 3-0, the Raiders will host an AFC West showdown with the fellow 3-0 Chiefs next weekend.

The 1-2 Saints will host the 1-2 Falcons next Monday night.

item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson left Sunday's game in the first quarter with an ankle injury and did not return before the end of Minnesota's 23-16 win over the Buccaneers.
item.content:encoded:
Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson left Sunday's game in the first quarter with an ankle injury and did not return before the end of Minnesota's 23-16 win over the Buccaneers.

At a postgame press conference, head coach Kevin O'Connell said that Jefferson "got close" to returning to the game but was ultimately ruled out. O'Connell also said that Jefferson will be evaluated more on Monday.

Mike Florio reported on Football Night in America that an MRI will be part of that evaluation and that the Vikings hope Jefferson is dealing with a low-ankle injury.

Jefferson had two catches for 32 yards before leaving the game. He has 13 catches for 179 yards and two touchdowns on the season,.

item.title: Cowboys take 28-24 lead after fourth-down stop of Ravens
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Cowboys were dead in the water, thisclose to being down 10 points.
item.content:encoded:
The Cowboys were dead in the water, thisclose to being down 10 points. But their beleaguered defense rose up when the Cowboys needed it most.

Rookie Jaishawn Barham and defensive tackle Otito Ogbonnia teamed up to keep Derrick Henry out of the end zone on a third-and-goal run from the 2. The play was initially ruled a touchdown but reversed on replay review.

The Ravens went for it on fourth down, and Braham met Henry in the backfield for a 3-yard loss.

The Cowboys needed only seven plays to go 96 yards, with KaVontae Turpin running it in from the 9. They have scored the last 15 points to take a 28-24 lead.

The Ravens led 24-13 before Jake Ferguson's 19-yard touchdown reception.

Dak Prescott is 22-of-33 for 240 yards and a touchdown, with CeeDee Lamb catching six passes for 98 yards. George Pickens has seven receptions for 82 yards.

Javontae Williams has 19 carries for 98 yards and a touchdown.

item.title: 49ers improve to 3-0 with hard-fought win over Cardinals
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: It wasn't as easy as expected, but San Francisco managed to win at home against Arizona.
item.content:encoded:
In the first two weeks of the season, the 49ers dominated. In Week 3, they had to gut out a surprisingly tough win.

Despite the 49ers jumping out to a 14-0 lead, the Cardinals weren't going to go down without a fight, and the game was close until the final moments, when the 49ers finally finished out a 36-30 win.

San Francisco quarterback Brock Purdy turned in another strong game, throwing for 297 yards with four touchdown passes and no interceptions. Purdy also ran for a 45-yard touchdown late in the game, although that touchdown was called back and turned into only a 35-yard gain because George Kittle was holding deep downfield.

Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett also deserves credit for his performance in a losing effort, throwing two touchdown passes and keeping the game close deep into the fourth quarter.

The injury-prone 49ers lost wide receiver Mike Evans with a rib injury, which has to be a big concern. They also saw left tackle Trent Williams leave with a stinger, although he was back on the sideline in the second half and looked OK.

The 49ers also may be concerned about kicker Eddy Pineiro, who hit a 57-yard field goal but also missed two extra points.

At 3-0, the 49ers are one of the best teams in the NFL. The 1-2 Cardinals are playing better than people expected, but they're still a distant fourth in the NFC West.

item.title: Sean McVay didn't have much to say after Sunday night's loss
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Anyone hoping to hear a detailed breakdown of why the Rams blew a 16-point halftime lead in Sunday night's loss to the Broncos was left disappointed by head coach Sean McVay's postgame press conference.
item.content:encoded:
Anyone hoping to hear a detailed breakdown of why the Rams blew a 16-point halftime lead in Sunday night's loss to the Broncos was left disappointed by head coach Sean McVay's postgame press conference.

McVay spent about 90 seconds on the podium after the 30-26 loss in Denver and fielded a couple of questions before signing off. The answers to those questions didn't provide much insight into what went wrong for the Rams.

“It’s tough, you know what, but this is sports," McVay said. "You sign up for all of it. Love our group, just came up short. Give the Broncos credit, they found a way to get it done. We’ll look at ourselves and figure out how we can improve.”

Media members covering the Rams noted that McVay started his press conference before most of them had made it down from the press box — reporters are informed that they should begin making their way down with five minutes left in the game, but it's up to them whether to do it — and that he wrapped it up as they were getting into the room. That's unusual for McVay, who usually has a fair amount to say after games and the brevity may be a sign of how disappointed he was in how the team performed while falling to 1-2 on the season.

item.title: Drake Maye attributes fumble to blood on the ball
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Patriots quarterback Drake Maye had an unusual moment on Sunday, when he cocked his arm to throw and his hand came forward without the ball in it.
item.content:encoded:
Patriots quarterback Drake Maye had an unusual moment on Sunday, when he cocked his arm to throw and his hand came forward without the ball in it.

After the game, Maye had an unusual explanation for it.

"[Center] Jared [Wilson] happened to be bleeding on his hand," Maye said. "Got the football and was trying to put one to [receiver] Kyle [Wiliams]. And [it] slipped out of my hand."

It's a twist on Brucie from The Longest Yard, when he attributed his lost grip on the ball to just eating popcorn. Either way, Patriots fans were likely choking on their popcorn while watching Maye's latest performance.

The Patriots are now 1-2. And they face the Bills in Buffalo next weekend.

item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Commanders linebacker Leo Chenal was put on a stretcher and carted off the field during Sunday's home win with a neck injury that will reportedly end his season.
item.content:encoded:
Commanders linebacker Leo Chenal was put on a stretcher and carted off the field during Sunday's home win with a neck injury that will reportedly end his season.

Chenal could be seen moving his arms and legs as he was on his way out of the stadium, but multiple reports on Monday say that he needs surgery that will keep him off the field for the rest of the year. NFL reporter Jordan Schultz had the initial report about the surgery and reported that Chenal suffered a fracture in his neck.

The injury occurred when Chenal dropped his head to tackle Seahawks running back Emanuel Wilson. He stayed down after the play and was surrounded by teammates as medical personnel responded to the situation.

Chenal signed with the Commanders this offseason after spending four years with the Chiefs. He had 18 tackles this season.

item.title: Colts kick late FG to pull out 19-17 win over Texans
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Colts kicker Spencer Shrader, who injured his groin in pregame warmups, ended up playing the part of hero.
item.content:encoded:
Colts kicker Spencer Shrader, who injured his groin in pregame warmups, ended up playing the part of hero. He kicked field goals of 39, 58, 37 and 53 in the Colts' 19-17 victory over the Texans.

His final field goal came with 16 seconds left.

The Colts are now 1-2, while the Texans fell to 0-3 for the second consecutive season. Houston rallied to make the playoffs last season, but the odds are against them to do it again.

The Colts, who led 13-7 at halftime and 16-7 midway through the fourth quarter, had the lead until 1:48 remained. C.J. Stroud directed a seven-play, 54-yard drive with Woody Marks scoring on a 1-yard run.

The Texans, though, botched the kickoff, with Ka'imi Fairbairn kicking it into the end zone. That allowed the Colts to start their game-winning drive at their own 35. DeMeco Ryans then botched the clock management, failing to use his first timeout after Jonathan Taylor's run left more than a minute on the clock.

Ryans finally called the timeout with 29 seconds remaining. It left too little time for the Texans to get into field goal range, and Stroud's Hail Mary throw on the final play was both short and out of bounds.

The Colts outgained the Texans 300 to 223 yards, with Daniel Jones going 24-of-36 for 235 yards with a touchdown and an interception. He also lost two fumbles, though the Texans turned it over on downs after the first one.

Jonathan Taylor had 23 carries for 68 yards, and Josh Downs caught five passes for 77 yards.

Adetomiwa Adebawore and DeForest Buckner each had 1 1/2 sacks of Stroud.

Stroud was 16-of-27 for 167 yards and a touchdown. David Montgomery had 11 carries for 33 yards, and Xavier Hutchinson caught three passes for 51 yards.

Texans defensive end Will Anderson had 2.5 sacks of Jones.

item.title: Sean Payton: We have to find a way to play better earlier
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Broncos were down 16-0 against the Rams at halftime on Sunday night, but they put up 30 points in the final 30 minutes to close out the game with their second straight win.
item.content:encoded:
The Broncos were down 16-0 against the Rams at halftime on Sunday night, but they put up 30 points in the final 30 minutes to close out the game with their second straight win.

The first of those wins played out in similar fashion. The Jaguars led the Broncos 13-3 in Week 2, but Denver rallied to score the final 17 points of the game and the two wins now give them 10 fourth quarter comeback wins since Bo Nix became the team's starting quarterback.

After the game, Payton said he likes that Nix is at his best in those moments but he believes that the Broncos "have to find a way to play better earlier" because continually falling behind is a recipe for disaster in the long term.

"I'm pleased with how we responded," Payton said. "We can't, like — it’ll cost us in bigger games against teams that are playing better later in the season. It will be something we're frustrated about later if we can't clean it up."

Next week's trip to visit the 3-0 49ers would be a good time for the Broncos to show they can hit the ground running rather than giving the opposition a sizable head start.

item.title: Sunday Night Football: Broncos complete comeback, defeat Rams 30-26
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Los Angeles was in it until the last play, but Denver was able to hang on for the team's second victory of the season.
item.content:encoded:
After getting blanked in the first half, the Broncos put together a strong final 30 minutes, eventually hanging on to beat the Rams 30-26.

Down 16-0 at halftime, the Broncos stormed back with two touchdowns and two-point conversions to tie the game at 16-16 with 2:15 left in the third period.

But even as the Rams took a three-point lead with 8:40 left in the fourth quarter, the Broncos were able to take advantage of every Los Angeles mistake to win.

On third-and-6 from the Denver 38, quarterback Matthew Stafford was picked off by Talanoa Hufanga and returned for a 66-yard pick-six, giving the Broncos a 23-19 lead.

That pick-six was the 33rd of Stafford’s career, breaking a tie with Brett Favre for the most in league history.

But Stafford was able to shake it off, coming right back with a 48-yard touchdown pass to Konata Mumpfield to make the score 26-23 with 3:38 left.

Rams penalties allowed the Broncos to go up by the final margin with under 60 seconds in the fourth quarter. While it looked like Josh Wallace had made his second interception, a questionable defensive pass interference penalty wiped the pick off the board and kept Denver’s possession going. Reviewing the play, NBC analyst Terry McAuley noted that it looked like receiver Pat Bryant pulled Wallace down rather than Wallace interfering with the receiver.

An illegal hands to the face penalty gave the Broncos another first down at the 2-yard line.

A couple of plays later, Nix dove into the end zone for a 1-yard, go-ahead touchdown.

The Rams were in it until the end, getting deep into Denver territory to spike the ball and stop the clock with two seconds left. But Stafford’s pass from the 19 to Davante Adams was intercepted by Hufanga, ending the game.

Nix finished the contest 17-of-34 for 186 yards with two touchdowns and an interception. Pat Bryant and Nate Adkins caught Nix’s TDs.

Stafford — who also became the first player in league history to throw for 20,000 yards for two teams in the first half — finished 30-of-55 for 390 yards with two touchdowns and two interceptions. Adams registered seven receptions for 137 yards, recording back-to-back 100-yard games with the Rams for the first time.

In his second game back from retirement, Aaron Donald had just one tackle and one QB hit.

As a whole, the Rams had just one sack and three QB hits.

The Broncos’ defense was particularly active around Stafford in the second half, registering a total of 14 QB hits in the game and five sacks. The unit also registered eight tackles for loss.

Now at 2-1, the Broncos will be on the road to face the 3-0 49ers in Week 4.

The 1-2 Rams will travel across the country to play the Eagles next Sunday.
